doseSections.title: Dosing
doseSections.text:
Dosing
ketorolac Use of IV ketorolac should be restricted to patients unable to receive enteral ibuprofen, naproxen or celecoxib *All IV orders must be reassessed at 48 hours and medication must be re-ordered if deemed appropriate to continue therapy. Lowest effective dose and shortest duration of administration minimizes risk of adverse effects. Ketorolac may increase risk for GI bleed especially in patients with multiple risk factors. Concurrent therapy with a PPI may decrease, but not eliminate, the risk for GI bleed.

doseSections.text:
IWK - 4.07 - Care of Patients on Opioid Agonist Treatment (OAT) [methadone, buPRENorphine/naloxone (Suboxone®)] for Opioid Use Disorder / Induction Phase
2−4 mg as an initial supervised dose when the patient is in moderate to severe withdrawal (Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale (COWS) greater than 13). Up to 6 mg is acceptable in clinically required situations, but may increase the risk of precipitating withdrawal.

doseSections.title: Dose information
doseSections.text:
Dose information
Reassess the patient after one to three hours and prescribe additional observed doses if necessary (e.g., COWS greater than 8, symptoms of withdrawal).

doseSections.title: Dose information
doseSections.text:
Dose information
Avoid prescribing more than 12 mg total on the first day.

doseSections.title: Dose information
doseSections.text:
Dose information
Be careful not to precipitate withdrawal by giving too high a dose or by medicating in the absence of observable withdrawal.

doseSections.title: Dose information
doseSections.text:
Dose information
One or two 2 mg tablets to take home may be provided if repeated observation is not feasible in the clinical setting, with clear instructions on timing the dose to avoid precipitating withdrawal.

doseSections.title: Consider alternative induction approaches such as:
doseSections.text:
Consider alternative induction approaches such as:
“microdosing,” starting with 0.5 mg twice per day, with increasing doses to a total daily dosage of 12 mg over 5–7 days for patients who cannot tolerate the significant period of abstinence needed to start with a conventional induction “rapid microdosing,” administering 0.5–1 mg at shorter intervals, up to 12 mg total in a 24-hour period.

doseSections.title: Titration and Stabilization Phase
doseSections.text:
Titration and Stabilization Phase
Add up the dose given on day 1 and administer it as the first dose of day 2, followed by additional doses based on the re-emergence of withdrawal symptoms. On day 3, add up the doses administered on day 2 and provide additional doses as necessary. Repeat daily until the patient is stable (no withdrawal, or COWS scores < 8 for 24 hours) or until a maximum of 24 mg per day is achieved.

doseSections.title: Maintenance
doseSections.text:
Maintenance
Use clinical judgment to maintain an optimal individualized daily dose, which is up to a maximum of 24 mg per day.

doseSections.title: Dose information
doseSections.text:
Dose information
If exceeding 24 mg in exceptional circumstances, inform the patient that this is a departure from approved doses and that there is limited evidence of a benefit with doses higher than 24 mg (and possibly an increased risk of adverse events). Review the case with an experienced colleague before trialing a dose higher than 24 mg per day and attempt to reduce the dose to approved levels (as tolerated) once the OUD has stabilized.

doseSections.title: Dosing
doseSections.text:
Dosing
Comments Separate daily doses by at least 15 hours. Oral route ineffective, swallowed doses are not readily absorbed. If patient vomits, do not replace dose.

buPRENorphine|naloxone - [Suboxone]
All dosing is based on buPRENorphine component.

Opioid Use Disorder (OUD)
Dosing is individualized. For additional information refer to "CAMH Opioid Agonist Therapy: A Synthesis of Canadian Guidelines for
Treating Opioid Use Disorder"

Go to clinical order set IWKOAT "Opioid Agonist Treatment (OAT) [methadone, buPRENorphine/ naloxone (Suboxone®)] for Opioid Use
Disorder High Alert

IWK - 4.07 - Care of Patients on Opioid Agonist Treatment (OAT) [methadone, buPRENorphine/naloxone (Suboxone®)] for Opioid Use
Disorder

Induction Phase

2−4 mg as an initial supervised dose when the patient is in moderate to severe withdrawal (Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale (COWS)
greater than 13). Up to 6 mg is acceptable in clinically required situations, but may increase the risk of precipitating withdrawal.

Reassess the patient after one to three hours and prescribe additional observed doses if necessary (e.g., COWS greater than 8,
symptoms of withdrawal).

Avoid prescribing more than 12 mg total on the first day.

Be careful not to precipitate withdrawal by giving too high a dose or by medicating in the absence of observable withdrawal.

One or two 2 mg tablets to take home may be provided if repeated observation is not feasible in the clinical setting, with clear
instructions on timing the dose to avoid precipitating withdrawal.

Consider alternative induction approaches such as:

     “microdosing,” starting with 0.5 mg twice per day, with increasing doses to a total daily dosage of 12 mg over 5–7 days for patients
     who cannot tolerate the significant period of abstinence needed to start with a conventional induction
     “rapid microdosing,” administering 0.5–1 mg at shorter intervals, up to 12 mg total in a 24-hour period.

Titration and Stabilization Phase

Add up the dose given on day 1 and administer it as the first dose of day 2, followed by additional doses based on the re-emergence of
withdrawal symptoms. On day 3, add up the doses administered on day 2 and provide additional doses as necessary. Repeat daily until
the patient is stable (no withdrawal, or COWS scores < 8 for 24 hours) or until a maximum of 24 mg per day is achieved.

Maintenance

Use clinical judgment to maintain an optimal individualized daily dose, which is up to a maximum of 24 mg per day.

     If exceeding 24 mg in exceptional circumstances, inform the patient that this is a departure from approved doses and that there is
      limited evidence of a benefit with doses higher than 24 mg (and possibly an increased risk of adverse events).
     Review the case with an experienced colleague before trialing a dose higher than 24 mg per day and attempt to reduce the dose
      to approved levels (as tolerated) once the OUD has stabilized.

Comments
   Separate daily doses by at least 15 hours.
   Oral route ineffective, swallowed doses are not readily absorbed.
   If patient vomits, do not replace dose.

Nova Scotia College of Pharmacists:

     Opioid Agonist Maintenance Treatment Services
     Opioid Agonist Maintenance Treatment Services During the COVID-19 Pandemic

Repeat as needed; start infusion when recurrent depression occurs after effective bolus, with toxicology/PICU. name: Midazolam

linkedPlans.excerpt: Respiratory support: Position, suction, high-flow oxygen and bag-mask ventilation if needed; prepare for intubation after repeated benzodiazepines or refractory seizure, with PICU/anesthesia. Medications/treatments: First line: lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg) or midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IN/IM/buccal (max 10 mg; max 5 mg per nostril), repeat once after 5 min if required. If still seizing, give one second-line load: levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV (max 3000 mg), fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg IV (max 1000 mg PE), or phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV (max 1000 mg), per local algorithm. Medications/treatments: First line: lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg) or midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IN/IM/buccal (max 10 mg; max 5 mg per nostril), repeat once after 5 min if required. linkedPlans.excerpt: Respiratory support: High-flow oxygen and early ventilatory support for respiratory failure; prepare for perioperative airway if source control is needed. Consider IVIG for refractory streptococcal toxic shock with ID/PICU. Urgent surgical debridement/source control is essential. Dosing
ciprofloxacin Ciprofloxacin suspension should NOT be given via an enteral feeding tube (e.g. g-tube) route. Crushed whole or portioned ciprofloxacin (regular) tablets can be given via tube, but should not be administered concurrently with enteral feedings. Discontinue feed for 1 to 2 hours prior to and after ciprofloxacin administration. Doses may be need to be adjusted to allow for the use of tablets (e.g. 1/4 of 250 mg tab = 62.5 mg)

       For anticipated duration of therapy more than 2 days monitor serum gentamicin levels as follows.

Timing of Serum Samples

      Serum concentrations should be measured at steady state, usually with the 3rd or 4th dose.
               Pre (trough): 0-30 minutes prior to dose
               Post (peak): 30 minutes after the end of a 30 minute IV infusion or 1 hour following IM injection

NOTE: Careful documentation of infusion and serum sample collection time is required. When interpreting levels, ensure timing of serum samples
is appropriate.

Target Serum Concentrations
                                                          Desired (micrograms/mL)
                 Indication                                Pre (trough) |           Post (Peak)
Synergy for Gram Positive Infections                        Less than 2     |          3-5
Urinary Tract Infection & Mild-Moderate Infections           Less than 2        |       4-8
Severe Infections (Pneumonia, Sepsis, CF)                   Less than 2 |             8-12

Suggested Regimen Adjustments based on Serum Concentration Results
Result           Adjustment
High Pre           ↑ Interval

High Post           ↓ Dose*
Low Post        ↑ Dose*
*Aminoglycosides exhibit linear kinetics. Decreasing or increasing the dose by a specified percentage will result in an equal decrease/increase in
percentage of peak levels.

Repeat levels with 3rd or 4th dose after regimen adjustments to ensure the desired results have been achieved and approximately every 7 days or
sooner if changing renal function or clinical status.

Peritonitis
Intraperitoneally

Go to 2012 ISPD Consensus Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of Catheter-Related Infections an Peritonitis in Pediatrics

doseStatus: Requires local formulary verification
administration: Injection 50 mg/mL. For IV intermittent infusion, dilute to a usual concentration of 5 mg/mL and infuse over 1 hour. Compatible solutions listed by CHEO include D5W, 0.9% sodium chloride, and lactated Ringer solution.
monitoring: Measure baseline serum creatinine. Monitor urine output, urinalysis, BUN/serum creatinine, liver enzymes, CBC, and accurate intake/output. Maintain adequate hydration during administration and for at least 2 hours afterward.
warnings: Acyclovir can precipitate in the kidneys if infused too rapidly, at high concentration, or in dehydration. Use ideal body weight for obese patients receiving IV therapy. Adjust the interval/dose in renal impairment.

linkedPlans.excerpt: Respiratory support: Oxygen to the hospital target. For severe refractory disease give magnesium sulfate 40-75 mg/kg IV over 20-30 min (max 2.5 g). name: Dexamethasone

linkedPlans.excerpt: Respiratory support: Oxygen to the hospital target. Salbutamol by MDI/spacer: <20 kg 5 puffs (500 mcg), >=20 kg 10 puffs (1000 mcg), or nebulized 2.5 mg/5 mg respectively; repeat/space by pathway. Add ipratropium for the first 3 severe treatments. Medications/treatments: Give systemic steroid early: dexamethasone 0.3-0.6 mg/kg PO/IV once (max 10-16 mg per local order set) or prednisone/prednisolone 1-2 mg/kg/day (max 50 mg). For severe refractory disease give magnesium sulfate 40-75 mg/kg IV over 20-30 min (max 2.5 g). Respiratory support: Keep child upright and calm; blow-by oxygen if needed. Avoid forcing a mask. Prepare difficult-airway equipment if severe. For stridor at rest give nebulized racemic epinephrine 2.25% 0.5 mL diluted to ~3 mL, or L-epinephrine 1 mg/mL 5 mL, according to available product; reassess promptly and observe at least 2-3 h after the last dose. Respiratory support: Keep upright with caregiver and provide gentle blow-by oxygen. Do not agitate, force supine positioning, use tongue depressor, or send an unstable child unaccompanied to imaging. doseSections.title: Dosing
doseSections.text:
Dosing
0.3 mg/kg/dose PO daily . Adjust dose according to serum drug levels Comments Younger children typically require higher mg/kg doses than older children and adults IV to PO conversion: total daily IV dose x 4 then divided every 12 hours PO Extended release dosage form: Monitor daily AM trough and adjust dose every ~2-3 days until target range Crossover may be considered for stable patients on immediate release formulation with no rejection for 3-6 months. Crossover ratio is 1:1. Single daily dose of extended release formulation equivalent to the patient's previous stable daily dose of immediate release formulation. Recommended to increase extended release formulation dose by 10-30% at time of conversion based on anticipated drop in AUC seen in clinical practice. IWK Nephrology target trough level ranges (time from renal transplant): less than 1 month: 10-12 ng/mL 1 to 2 months: 8-12 ng/mL 3 to 6 months: 7-10 ng/mL 6 to 12 months: 5-8 ng/mL greater than 12 months: 4-8 ng/mL (ideally 5-7 ng/mL) NOTE: If confirmed nephrotoxicity or EBV mismatch, target ranges may be lower If confirmed rejection, target ranges may be higher

linkedPlans.excerpt: Respiratory support: Position, suction, high-flow oxygen and bag-mask ventilation if needed; prepare for intubation after repeated benzodiazepines or refractory seizure, with PICU/anesthesia. Medications/treatments: First line: lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg) or midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IN/IM/buccal (max 10 mg; max 5 mg per nostril), repeat once after 5 min if required. If still seizing, give one second-line load: levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV (max 3000 mg), fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg IV (max 1000 mg PE), or phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV (max 1000 mg), per local algorithm. doseSections.text:
carglumic acid - [Carbaglu] / Renal Adjustment .
Comments Oral Administration Using an Oral Syringe in Pediatric Patients: • Mix each 200 mg tablet in 2.5 ml of water to yield a concentration of 80 mg/ml in a mixing container. Shake gently to allow for quick dispersal; • Draw up the mixture in an oral syringe and administer immediately. Pieces of the tablet may remain in the oral syringe. • Refill the oral syringe with a minimum volume of water (1 to 2 mL) and administer immediately. • Flush the oral syringe again, as needed, until no pieces of the tablet are left in the syringe. Nasogastric (NG tube) or Gastrostomy (G-tube) administration: It is recommended to divide the total daily dose into two to four doses to be given before feedings. For patients who have a NG tube or G-tube in place, CARBAGLU should be administered as follows: Pediatrics • Mix each 200 mg tablet in 2.5 ml of water to yield a concentration of 80 mg/ml in a mixing container. Shake gently to allow for quick dispersal; • Draw up the appropriate volume of dispersion and administer immediately through the NG tube or G-tube. Discard the unused portion; • Flush with additional water to clear the NG tube or G-tube

doseSections.title: Lennox–Gastaut syndrome
doseSections.text: Start 10 mg/kg/day PO divided twice daily; increase every other day toward 45 mg/kg/day divided twice daily (maximum 3.2 g/day). Give with food. Shortens QT; specialist-directed.

doseSections.title: Focal/generalized seizures
doseSections.text: Start 1–2 mg/kg/day PO once daily or divided twice daily; titrate every 1–2 weeks. Usual 4–8 mg/kg/day; maximum commonly 12 mg/kg/day or 600 mg/day. Monitor bicarbonate, renal stones, sweating/heat intolerance, and sulfonamide reactions.

doseSections.title: Dravet, Lennox–Gastaut, or tuberous-sclerosis seizures
doseSections.text: Start 2.5 mg/kg/dose PO twice daily; after 1 week increase to 5 mg/kg/dose twice daily. Further titration and maximum depend on indication (commonly 10 mg/kg/dose twice daily). Monitor liver enzymes, sedation, and clobazam interactions.

linkedPlans.excerpt: Respiratory support: Oxygen if hypoxemic or poorly perfused; prepare for sedation/airway support if cardioversion is required. Unstable SVT: synchronized cardioversion 0.5-1 J/kg, then 2 J/kg if needed. Further antiarrhythmic therapy is cardiology/PICU-directed. protamine
Heparin Inf usion Antidote
If anticoagulation needs to be terminated, discontinuation of heparin infusion will usually suffice. If an immediate effect is required,
consider administering protamine. Following IV administration, neutralization occurs within 5 minutes

                  Time Since End of IV Heparin Infusion                   Dose of Protamine (mg) to Neutralize 100 units of Heparin*
                                 (min)
                               less than 30                                                               1
                                  30-60                                                               0.5-0.75
                                 61-120                                                               0.375-0.5
                            greater than 120                                                         0.25-0.375
*Heparin received within previous 2 hours
Maximum: 50 mg/dose

Subcutaneous Heparin Antidote
1 mg protamine neutralizes ~100 units of heparin. Give a portion of the total dose by slow IV injection then give the remainder of the
dose by IV infusion over 8-16 hours

Maximum: 50 mg TOTAL DOSE

Low Molecular Weight Heparin (LMWH) antidote
If anticoagulation needs to be terminated, discontinuation of LMWH injections will usually suffice. If an immediate reversal of effect is
required, protamine reverses some (60-75%) of the anti-Factor Xa activity of LMWH. Haematology Service must be consulted for
recommendations.

If LMWH dose has been administered within the last 8 hours
Use 1 mg protamine per 1 mg (or 100 units) LMWH. If PTT (activated) remains prolonged 2-4 hours after first dose, a second dose of 0.5
mg protamine per 1 mg (or 100 units) LMWH may be given.

Maximum: 50 mg/dose
Comments
   Patients with known hypersensitivity reaction to fish or those who have had previous protamine therapy, may be at risk for
   hypersensitivity reaction to protamine.
   Heparin rebound with bleeding may occur 8-18 hours after protamine administration.

Supplied: Injection: 10 mg/mL

name: Regular insulin

linkedPlans.excerpt: Respiratory support: Oxygen only if needed; avoid routine bicarbonate. If consciousness declines, protect airway with PICU/anesthesia while avoiding hypocapnia from excessive ventilation. Medications/treatments: Start regular insulin infusion 0.05-0.1 units/kg/h after at least 1 h of fluids; no insulin bolus. Add potassium to IV fluids once urine output/renal function and serum potassium permit. For suspected cerebral injury give 3% saline 5 mL/kg over 10-15 min (max 250 mL) or mannitol 0.5-1 g/kg promptly and call PICU. Medications/treatments: Start regular insulin infusion 0.05-0.1 units/kg/h after at least 1 h of fluids; no insulin bolus. Add potassium to IV fluids once urine output/renal function and serum potassium permit. For suspected cerebral injury give 3% saline 5 mL/kg over 10-15 min (max 250 mL) or mannitol 0.5-1 g/kg promptly and call PICU.

Respiratory support: As needed; prepare resuscitation equipment if ECG changes or instability are present. Medications/treatments: Stop potassium sources. With ECG change or severe hyperkalemia give calcium gluconate 10% 0.5-1 mL/kg IV (max 10 mL) with monitoring; shift potassium with regular insulin 0.1 units/kg IV plus dextrose, nebulized salbutamol and bicarbonate only for significant acidosis. Remove potassium with diuretic/resin/dialysis as appropriate; use local emergency protocol and pharmacy double check. Medications/treatments: Stop potassium sources. doseSections.title: Dose information
doseSections.text:
Dose information
Comments * Single doses greater than 15 grams have been used, but are not recommended and are unlikely to increase potassium removal (Source: Moffett, Lee 2016) . Excessive dosage or inadequate dilution could result in impaction of the resin.

doseSections.title: Dosing
doseSections.text:
Dosing
Dosing may also be based on 1 gram of resin binding with ~ 1 mEq potassium. Releases 1 mEq sodium per gram for each 1 mEq potassium removed. Powder: each 1 gram of powder equals 1.3 mL when measured in an oral syringe. Mix each gram of powder with 3-4 mL water for oral administration. Suspension: may be given PO, NG, PR. After rectal administration, irrigate colon thoroughly to ensure adequate removal of resin.

summary: First-line antiemetic for selected pediatric vomiting syndromes. For acute gastroenteritis, evidence supports a single oral dose to facilitate oral rehydration rather than scheduled multidose therapy.
doseStatus: Route- and indication-specific dose sections available — verify locally
administration: PO/ODT preferred for gastroenteritis when tolerated; begin oral rehydration 15–30 minutes later. IV use is indication- and setting-specific. Verify formulation and concentration.
monitoring: Assess hydration and response. ECG/electrolytes are not routinely required before one oral dose in a low-risk child, but review QTc, potassium, magnesium and interacting QT-prolonging drugs when risk factors, repeated dosing, IV therapy or medication stacking are present.
warnings: QT prolongation; headache, constipation, and diarrhea. Avoid or obtain specialist review in congenital long-QT syndrome. Correct significant hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia and avoid casual combination with other QT-prolonging drugs.

doseSections.title: Dosing
doseSections.text:
Dosing
Some patients may need increased doses up to 30 mg po BID if they remain symptomatic. Higher doses may be ordered in consultation with GI services. Prevacid FasTab® cannot be split: tablets are not scored and dose is not distributed evenly through the tablet. Do not chew or crush capsules or FasTab®. Capsules can be opened and mixed in 60 mL of an acidic beverage (juice) or granules can be sprinkled over soft food (i.e applesauce, yogurt, cottage cheese or pudding) For administration via oral syringe, or NG tube greater than or equal to 8 French, Prevacid FasTab® can be administered as follows: Place a 15 mg tablet in oral syringe and draw up approximately 4 mL of water, or place a 30 mg tablet in oral syringe and draw up approximately 10 mL of water. Shake gently to allow for a quick dispersal. After the tablet has dispersed, administer the contents within 15 minutes. Refill the syringe with approximately 2 mL (5 mL for the 30 mg tablet) of water, shake gently, and administer any remaining contents.

For intentional overdose, institute suicide precautions, secure medications/unsafe belongings and arrange mental-health/social-work assessment after medical stabilization. name: Activated charcoal

linkedPlans.excerpt: Medications/treatments: Call provincial poison centre early. Use specific antidote/decontamination only when indicated; activated charcoal requires protected airway and correct timing. Treat seizures, dysrhythmias and sodium-channel blockade per toxicology protocol.

Discuss activated charcoal with Ontario Poison Centre. Consider single-dose activated charcoal for a potentially toxic ingestion when presentation is early enough to provide benefit and the airway is protected with no bowel obstruction or major aspiration risk. Poison Centre may recommend charcoal later after a massive ingestion, extended-release product or opioid/anticholinergic co-ingestion because absorption may be delayed. Never delay NAC when NAC is indicated.
NPO. Do not induce vomiting, neutralize the substance or give activated charcoal. Avoid blind nasogastric insertion.
Contact the Ontario Poison Centre immediately. Activated charcoal, serum/urine alkalinization and hemodialysis are indication-specific and must follow toxicology/nephrology guidance.
Contact Poison Centre immediately. Whole-bowel irrigation and deferoxamine are indication-specific. Activated charcoal does not bind iron effectively.

Supportive care. Activated charcoal is generally avoided because aspiration risk outweighs benefit. Antibiotics and corticosteroids are not routinely indicated unless a separate bacterial infection or other indication emerges.

name: Hydroxyurea

linkedPlans.excerpt: Medications/treatments: Start tumor-lysis prophylaxis/treatment with hematology—rasburicase for high risk/raised uric acid or allopurinol for selected lower risk. Cytoreduction (steroid, hydroxyurea, chemotherapy or leukapheresis) is hematology-directed. Treat fever as febrile neutropenia/sepsis.

Medications/treatments: Start analgesia within 30 min: acetaminophen/NSAID when safe plus opioid for moderate-severe pain using the individualized plan; reassess and repeat/titrate every 20-30 min until controlled. Continue hydroxyurea unless contraindicated. Incentive spirometry q2h while awake; avoid overhydration.

name: Thiamine

linkedPlans.excerpt: Fluids: Correct deficit carefully; nutrition advancement with phosphate/potassium/magnesium/thiamine plan when severe malnutrition.
Start nutrition gradually using a dietitian-led pathway. Replace phosphate, potassium, magnesium and thiamine according to current local protocols; avoid unsupervised generic replacement.

Treat malnutrition/refeeding risk and optimize enteral nutrition carefully. Do not rapidly increase calories in a high-risk patient until phosphate, potassium, magnesium and thiamine management are established.

Give thiamine before or with initiation of nutrition according to the local pediatric protocol. Replace phosphate, potassium and magnesium proactively or therapeutically based on levels and risk. Do not delay urgently needed nutrition indefinitely, but slow/hold advancement and intensify replacement/monitoring if electrolytes fall or organ dysfunction develops. Dietitian and the relevant admitting service; adolescent medicine/eating-disorder team when applicable; pharmacy for electrolyte/thiamine therapy; PICU, cardiology, nephrology or endocrinology according to severity.

name: Mannitol

linkedPlans.excerpt: Medications/treatments: Start regular insulin infusion 0.05-0.1 units/kg/h after at least 1 h of fluids; no insulin bolus. Add potassium to IV fluids once urine output/renal function and serum potassium permit. For suspected cerebral injury give 3% saline 5 mL/kg over 10-15 min (max 250 mL) or mannitol 0.5-1 g/kg promptly and call PICU.

Fluids/diet: Start isotonic IV crystalloid, commonly 1.5-2 times maintenance and titrate to urine output/clinical status; avoid potassium-containing fluids initially. Routine bicarbonate/mannitol is not recommended without a specific indication.

name: Insulin regular high-dose therapy

linkedPlans.excerpt: Call Poison Centre immediately. Initial therapy may include atropine for symptomatic bradycardia, glucagon, vasopressors and high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy; exact dosing and sequencing must follow the Ontario Poison Centre beta-blocker algorithm and local PICU/pharmacy protocol. Treat seizures with benzodiazepines; consider sodium bicarbonate for propranolol-associated QRS widening and lipid emulsion only when toxicology recommends.

Call Poison Centre immediately. Treatment may include IV calcium, vasopressors and high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy; exact agent, dose and targets must follow the Ontario Poison Centre calcium-channel blocker algorithm. Consider whole-bowel irrigation for selected modified-release ingestions and lipid emulsion or ECMO only after toxicology/PICU consultation.
